RagShortTexts: The Rurikid dynasty preserved Rus princely bloodlines across fragmented principalities.

Variants.Content: The Rurikid dynasty traced its descent to Rurik the Varangian, and it held every Rus land under the falcon-trident tamga. The Mongol conquest of 1240 broke that unity into rival branches. Alexander Nevsky, ruling from Vladimir, chose stoic submission to the Golden Horde, which he judged the only way to protect Orthodox churches from destruction. Daniel of Galicia took a different path and accepted a papal crown, hoping for Western help in a war against the Tatars. Their choices split the dynasty along the line between Christian Europe and the Mongol khanate.

Khan's patents, known as yarlyks, decided who held the princely seats and settled succession disputes. Rurikid cousins travelled across the frozen steppe to Sarai with chests of sable furs, bidding against each other for the khan's favour. A prince who won a yarlyk gained the right to rule, and one who lost could find his lands handed to a rival.
The Orthodox Metropolitan of Kyiv, residing across northern towns, preserved ecclesiastical unity, counseling princes against fratricidal squabbling.
